matcher.note: matcher_differs is true where this release of the matcher does not give the expected result. Every other vector passes on it.

fields.id: A stable name for the vector. It never changes once published.
fields.robots_txt: The whole robots.txt file, as a string. Line ends are part of the test.
fields.user_agent: The product token of the crawler asking.
fields.path: The path and query of the URL to test, as the crawler would request it.
fields.expected: allowed or disallowed, as RFC 9309 reads the file.
fields.decided_by: The rule that decides the result: its line number in robots_txt, counted from 1, and its text without a comment. null when no rule decides: no rule matched, no group applied, or the path is /robots.txt.
fields.group: Which group the crawler obeys: own (a group that names it), * (the * group) or none.
fields.rfc: The section of RFC 9309 the vector tests, and the sentence it tests, word for word. level is the requirement keyword in that sentence, or null when it has none.
fields.reason: Why the result follows, in a sentence or two.
fields.from: Where the vector comes from. tool-test is a test of answer-crawler-check, named in test. rfc is an example or a sentence of RFC 9309. sandbox is the list of differences on the robots.txt sandbox page.
fields.matcher_differs: true when release 0.1.2 of the answer-crawler-check matcher gives the other result.
fields.difference: Present when matcher_differs is true. The id of the difference in the differences list.

differences.summary: The matcher compares a percent-encoded unreserved character as written. A rule for /private does not match the path /%70rivate, and RFC 9309 says it should.
The matcher ends a run of user-agent lines at a line that is not a rule, such as Crawl-delay. The names above that line get none of the rules below it. RFC 9309 keeps them in one group.

rfc.quote: Crawlers MUST use case-insensitive matching to find the group that matches the product token and then obey the rules of the group.

vectors.reason: ExampleBot has a group of its own, so it obeys that group and not the * group.

from.test: a named group overrides the wildcard group entirely

rfc.quote: If no matching group exists, crawlers MUST obey the group with a user-agent line with the "*" value, if present.

vectors.reason: No group names OtherBot, so it obeys the * group.

from.test: a named group overrides the wildcard group entirely

rfc.quote: If no match is found amongst the rules in a group for a matching user-agent or there are no rules in the group, the URI is allowed.

vectors.reason: The rule for /private/ is in the * group. ExampleBot obeys only its own group, where no rule matches.

from.test: a named group does not inherit the wildcard rules

rfc.quote: Crawlers MUST use case-insensitive matching to find the group that matches the product token and then obey the rules of the group.

vectors.reason: The group names examplebot in lower case, and the name still matches ExampleBot.

from.test: agent names match case-insensitively and by product token
